newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Jan 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Jan 6.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Monday:
- Virtually all the hundreds of Web sites set up by the nation's newspapers still do not take full advantage of one of the Internet's most compelling features: immediacy.
- The makers and sellers of personal computers hope to get a lift Wednesday when Intel Corp introduces a new version of its Pentium microprocessor.
- Silicon Graphics has missed analysts estimates for five consecutive quarters, and Wall Street is holding its breath for the December-quarter results.
- With the death of Harry Helmsley, his wife Leona Helmsley may quickly lose control of Helmsley-Spear, the company at the centre of the real estate empire that reaps an estimated $60 million a year.

- In their first public rift with the management team they helped pick, leaders of the pilots union at United Airlines have said that as a result of what they termed disappointing contract negotiations, they would no longer cooperate in trying to foster a collegial culture at the employee-owned company.
- With its disclosure that it expects losses of $100 million to $150 million in its first quarter, Apple Computer shows signs of a serious setback to efforts to revive itself.

- While library science remains a discipline dedicated to finding, filtering, organising, evaluating and presenting information, it now requires a great deal more technical expertise with electronic information and computer networks -- demands that, in turn, have opened a raft of new career opportunities.
- Twelve to 15 movies will be released this year at a cost of $100 million or more each. Never have so many films costing so much been released in a single year.
- The financial printing industry has embraced the very technologies that are threatening its core business.
- The World Wide Web is home to innumerable sources to help consumers choose travel and vacation destinations.
- For home-improving do-it-yourselfers and others confronted with noxious fumes, a new breathing system features a face mask and two tubes.
- World Wide Web voyeurism has evolved quite a bit from the days of cheap digital cameras shooting grainy black and white pictures of mundane objects, updated every few minutes.
